submission.natural_language_explanation: This direction fires where a clause's subject is plural: on the plural head noun or plural pronoun itself, on the rest of that subject phrase up to the token before the finite verb, and on a pre-verbal clitic, negation or adverb standing between a plural subject and its verb — 40-95% of max in French, Spanish, Portuguese and Italian and on German plural nouns with an overt plural ending ('Kinder', 'Forschungsschwerpunkte'), but only 10-15% of max, below the active line, on English and Dutch plural subjects. It is near zero for a singular subject with an ordinary predicate, for a plural noun in object position and for a plural noun inside a singular subject's prepositional phrase, and its write supports plural-agreeing predicate forms (ablating it costs ' ont', ' sont', ' peuvent', ' pueden', ' sono', ' waren', and its Jacobian lens promotes the Mandarin distributive 都/均) while suppressing English 3sg ' is'/' has'/' was', so it reads the subject's number rather than preparing one specific upcoming token.

rival_explanations: The direction is a plural-morphology detector rather than a subject tracker: it fires on any token that marks plurality, so plural objects ('El director leyó los informes', 'Les rapports') and plural nouns inside a singular subject's prepositional phrase should be as active as a plural subject.

It is a number-blind predicate-opening detector (the reading published for its member N4413), firing at the clitic, negation, modal or semi-auxiliary that opens a finite predicate whatever the subject's number, so 'Il doit partir demain matin' should match 'Ils doivent partir demain matin'.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial English plural pronoun We, the no-leading-space form of the claimed token ' We', with an ordinary past-tense predicate; the hypothesis says English plural subjects stay below the active line.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: De kinderen spelen buiten in de tuin terwijl hun ouders het avondeten koken.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dutch plural noun subject with an overt -en plural, the direct Dutch counterpart of the German 'Kinder' case the hypothesis does cover; the hypothesis says Dutch plural subjects are inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Zij kochten gisteren een nieuwe fiets bij de winkel op de hoek.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Dutch plural pronoun 'Zij', which contains the claimed fragment 'ij', used as subject with a lexical verb; the hypothesis puts Dutch plural subjects below the active line.
